head: afd021d2e231a732a596033c22af811201e6659d
summary:
The product change in attempt 3 is sound:

- The root is resolved string-first, with a handle fallback, so subst, 8.3, volume-GUID and symlink roots such as C:\Users\All Users map correctly. This answers m1.
- The FolderDone equality check never runs GetFullPath on children. This answers m2.
- Core decides the Refused outcome, which follows Q-179/Q-182.
- ScanArm's S and P arms read the listing arm's own file list. This answers N1's main hazard.
- The tag owners are recalled honestly and the findstr step is gone. This answers N6.
- The Fast Startup claim is labelled unmeasured. This answers N4.

The acceptance test will pass. N5 is moot because the unfixed arms are gone.

The rework silently drops several dispositions that were accepted and are still owed, and it introduces new defects in the protocol:

- **M5 (major):** NotScanned rows are now built by UnreadableRows.Build, and the report says nothing about how the excluded store appears. Nothing stops it reaching the report's unreadable list, read-denied-folders and the read-window counts. The accepted separate array and the m5 WindowCases case are both missing.
- **M3/N3 (major):** the pressure step is gone with no reason given. Outcome C again documents a Restart workaround from readings taken 10 min after exit, with nothing separating cache from leak.
- **New (major):** the dir controls cannot be kept out of the store by choosing sibling roots, because `dir /s` follows links. C:\Users\All Users is a directory symlink to C:\ProgramData, so the Q-178 dir of C:\Users walks the live layer. A layer subtree that contains a junction to C:\ProgramData does the same.
- **New (major):** R0 is defined twice: taken in -Prepare before the Restart, and as step 1 after it. Read literally, 'VOID if boot > 30 min old at R0' VOIDs every session after 4 hours.
- **New (major):** -Report has no outcome when the WC* or handle clause fails while pool is within T. That clause is the only measurement of the two must-verify preconditions (the store's siblings don't leak; no other path reaches the store).
  - Ambient is again a linear rate from I0/I1 rather than M6's burst-aware estimate per gap.
  - The outcome set has no UNDECIDED (m7).
- **M4 (major):** the unfixed arms are dropped, and m6's 'cancel after passing the store' is only partly kept.
- **N7/m3 (minor):** the rule patterns lost (?m), are case-sensitive, have no "Layers" literal pattern and no RunAs rule.

Minor items:
- the closing control's '≥1 WC*' threshold is too weak;
- where the `dir /a /s` store-size bound runs is not stated;
- under the test override, step 2 still opens %ProgramData%;
- 'Show in Explorer' on the NotScanned row invites the browsing the workaround forbids.

Citations: #646 and Q&A 5966064 were confirmed earlier. Windows-Sandbox#126 ties leaks to Sandbox sessions, which supports bursty rather than linear ambient. The link-following claims are confirmed by schneegans.de/windows/find-files, superuser.com/questions/528487 and stackoverflow.com/questions/6913784.

findings.claim: The accepted M5 disposition is walked past. The excluded store is now a NotScanned EntryKind that UnreadableRows.Build renders, the same builder as unreadable folders, and is only 'kept out of the could-not-be-opened count'. The design never says how the store appears in the schema-1 --report: no skippedStores array, and no statement that it is absent from the report's unreadable list. If the report's unreadable list is filled from UnreadableRows rows, as the shared builder suggests, the store path reaches the two consumers M5 named: the engine's read-denied-folders, which opens the listed paths with SeBackupPrivilege and counts their contents, and eng/read-window.ps1's counts. 'Kept out of the count' then becomes a filter every consumer has to remember. The m5 WindowCases case (scan ...\Containers with --report, assert the skip entry and an unchanged unreadable count) is also gone. Only the refused-root report case remains, and without a report representation for the skip it cannot be written.
findings.evidence: Component 'Not-scanned folder kind': 'UnreadableRows.Build shows it as a 'size not counted' row... keeps it out of the 'N folders could not be opened' count.' 'App refusal and report fields' adds only outcome "refused" and refusal "container-layer-store". M5 decision: 'a separate array in schema-1 --report, never into the unreadable list'. m5 decision: 'one WindowCases case that scans ...\Containers with --report and asserts the skip entry'.
findings.fix: State the report contract: a separate additive 'notScanned' array of {path, reason} in schema-1, and NotScanned rows never written to the report's unreadable list. Enforce it in the report writer by kind, not by consumers filtering. Restore the m5 WindowCases case on C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers, asserting one notScanned entry for Layers and an unreadable count without it.

findings.claim: The accepted M3 and N3 dispositions, a pressure step with a positive control whose failure makes outcome C UNDECIDED, are gone, and the design gives no reason. Readings are taken 10 min after exit with no pressure. If L's retention is FMfn/File/NtfF held until NTFS stream teardown, which is the mechanism the design's own cited source describes, L goes over T, the run routes to C, and the record documents 'Start > Restart' as the workaround for cache. That is the verdict both dispositions were accepted to prevent. The new 4096 MB Available guard does not justify dropping the step: N3's decision already said the step should stay above the guard.
findings.evidence: Protocol order: 'R0, I0, L, S, P, 5 full, 5 cancelled, I1, dir control' (no pressure step). Tolerance: 'Each reading is taken 10 min after the process exits.' Routing: 'L over T: C'... 'Otherwise it records FAIL, with the Restart workaround documented.' Q&A 5946136 title: 'FMfn paged-pool retention until NTFS stream teardown'. N3 decision: 'only holds longer or lowers the floor while staying above the existing abort guard... If no watched tag falls, the step is labelled INEFFECTIVE and outcome C becomes UNDECIDED'.
findings.fix: Restore -Pressure after the cancelled arms and before I1, with its floor above the 4096 MB guard. Restore its positive control in -Prepare (cold %TEMP% tree: mark, pressure, mark). Let -Report route to C only from post-pressure figures, and write UNDECIDED when the step is ineffective.

findings.claim: The design keeps its dir controls out of the live layer only by choosing which roots to hand to dir: 'issued per sibling root... never on an ancestor of the store'. But cmd's `dir /s` follows reparse-point directories, and C:\Users holds 'All Users', a directory symlink to C:\ProgramData. So the Q-178 dir of the sibling root C:\Users walks C:\Users\All Users\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers\<id>\Files. That leaks about 210K WC* entries and System handles, and pollutes the per-entry comparison it exists to make. The design's own words apply: 'the control itself would be the bug'. The same risk applies to the closing control. A layer subtree picked in -Prepare that contains a container-side junction such as ProgramData\Application Data, with the absolute target C:\ProgramData, resolves on the host to host ProgramData and walks the whole store.
findings.evidence: schneegans.de/windows/find-files/: 'C:\Users directory... contains both a symbolic link and a junction: <SYMLINKD> All Users [C:\ProgramData]'. superuser.com/questions/528487: 'the built-in dir takedown icacls commands run into an infinite loop with the Application Data directory'. stackoverflow.com/questions/6913784: `dir /s` in C:\Users\me lists 'Application Data\Application Data\...'. Design: 'Any dir control is issued per sibling root from the -Prepare list and never on an ancestor of the store.'
findings.fix: Issue every dir control through a walker that does not follow reparse-point directories, such as `robocopy <root> <nonexistent> /L /E /XJ`, or a .NET enumeration with AttributesToSkip=ReparsePoint. Verify in -Prepare, on the current already-touched boot, that it does not descend C:\Users\All Users. Have -Prepare also reject any closing-control subtree that contains a reparse-point directory.

findings.claim: R0 names two different readings. -Prepare, run before the Restart, 'takes R0', and protocol step 1 after the Restart is also 'R0'. The VOID rule ('the boot is more than 30 min old at R0') and the guard ('combined pool rises more than 4 GiB above R0') both key on R0. If built from -Prepare's reading, every session goes VOID at -Report time, after about 4 h and a spent Restart, and the guard sits 4 GiB above the pre-restart pool of about 8 GB instead of the fresh-boot baseline.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch component: '-Prepare, run BEFORE the Restart: builds ScanArm, publishes the exe and takes R0.' Key decision 8: '1. R0, then I0: 20 min idle.' Contract error_cases: 'The run is VOID if: the boot is more than 30 min old at R0'. Guard: 'combined pool rises more than 4 GiB above R0'.
findings.fix: Rename -Prepare's reading to Rpre, the pre-restart mark that settles Restart reclaim. Define R0 as the first reading after the Restart and key the VOID rule and the guard on it. Have -Protocol refuse to start, rather than VOID afterwards, when boot age exceeds 30 min.

findings.claim: PASS needs 'WC* allocations and System 0x120089 handles <= the ambient rate from I0 and I1'. When that clause fails while L, S and P are within T, no route applies: B and C are defined only by pool against T, so -Report has no outcome. This clause is the only measurement of the cross-domain transfer's two must-verify preconditions ('listing the store's parent and siblings does not trigger the leak'; 'no other path in a scan reaches the store's contents', for example BaseImages or another WCI tree that EntryClassifier enters on purpose). So if either precondition fails, the run ends with no verdict, or a reader treats it as A with one clause unmet. Ambient is also again a linear rate from two 20-minute windows about 4 h apart. Accepted M6 asked for drift per gap, aware of bursts. Windows-Sandbox#126 leaks per session, and the engine saw WCsc arrive in 2 of 37 intervals. So one burst during an arm fails the clause with no route. The outcome set (A, B, C, FAIL-cancel, VOID) also has no UNDECIDED, so accepted m7 (null input gives UNDECIDED) has nowhere to land.
findings.evidence: Key decision 7: PASS clauses and 'Otherwise the run routes as the spike set it: L over T: C. S over while P is within: B...'. cross_domain_transfer invariants 3 and 4: 'must-verify'. Decidable disagreement 2: 'The protocol's WC* clause measures it.' github.com/microsoft/Windows-Sandbox/issues/126: 'Every Windows Sandbox session causes the host's System process to accumulate kernel file handles'. M6 and m7 decisions.
findings.fix: Add an outcome WCIFS-UNATTRIBUTED. It is written when WC* or handles exceed the envelope of the gaps next to the arm, and it blocks A until a person looks. Estimate ambient per gap from the readings that already bracket each arm, leaving out bursts over 3× the median gap. Have ScanArm L write a progress log (timestamp, folder) and take a mark every 60 s during L, so a burst can be lined up with a subtree (the tail of N2). Add UNDECIDED to -Report's outcomes for null inputs (m7).

findings.claim: Two more accepted, still-owed dispositions are walked past with no reason given. (1) M4: there is no unfixed afd021d arm. Brief step 1's 'which case grows the pool' is never measured on the app as it was reported, and the only armability control is a non-app dir over 10-180 entries. (2) m6: the cancelled runs are now relative to a phase ('Cancel during listing x2...') with an offset or calibrated delay. Nothing guarantees a cancel lands after the walk has passed the store, which is what m6 required so that a cancelled run exercises the skip. m4's backstop also disappeared, but its accepted justification was M6's counter, which X5 covers, so m4 alone is moot. The build now has instructions from the dispositions that contradict this design.
findings.evidence: M4 decision: 'Add an unfixed arm built from `git archive afd021d` after the fixed arms... Its first completed scan becomes the positive control.' m6 decision: 'Set the cancel point from progress: after the scan has passed ProgramData... Record the folder count at cancel.' Design cancelled-run driver: 'phase-relative points... a delay variable, calibrated from the listing time'.
findings.fix: Either restore one unfixed completed scan and one unfixed cancelled scan after I1 and before the closing control (publish afd021d in -Prepare, mark them like the fixed runs), or record the person's decision that drops M4. For the listing-phase cancels, set the offset past the store: the hook fires a number of folders after the NotScanned row is recorded, and the folder count at cancel goes in the mark.

findings.claim: The accepted N7 (and m3) rule fixes are not in architecture_rules. Rule 1's patterns have no leading (?m), which eng/rules-parity.ps1:34-35 requires for twinned patterns (attempt 2 twinned every rule). They are case-sensitive, so a second copy written as "containers\\layers" works on Windows and passes. There is no pattern forbidding the literal "Layers". The PoolWatch*.ps1 rule with only the -Verb RunAs pattern was not restored, so nothing fails if the person-run script raises a UAC prompt mid-session.
findings.evidence: architecture_rules[0].must_not_match: 'Containers[\\/]{1,2}Layers', '"Containers"\s*,\s*"Layers"'. N7 decision: "'(?m)(?i:Containers[\\/]{1,2}Layers)' and '(?m)(?i:\"Layers\")'... Restore a PoolWatch*.ps1 rule containing only the -Verb RunAs pattern."
findings.fix: Use `(?m)(?i:Containers[\\/]{1,2}Layers)` and `(?m)(?i:"Layers")`, with ContainerLayerStore.cs excepted. Add the rule for tests/window/PoolWatch*.ps1 with `(?m)-Verb\s+['"]?RunAs\b`. Twin and plant each rule, with the fltmc paste prompt as the correct line that must not fire.

findings.claim: The closing control decides VOID on 'leaks >= 1 WC*' over 1-3 subtrees of 10-60 entries. Ambient wcifs activity comes in bursts, and the CmService zygote touches layer entries on its own. So a single ambient allocation during the control makes the layer look armable when the chosen subtrees were already touched. Picking arbitrary subtrees also risks ones the zygote touches at boot, which would VOID a 4-hour session.
findings.evidence: Contract: 'VOID if... the closing layer control leaks 0 WC*'. PASS clause: 'the closing layer control leaks >= 1 WC*'. Investigation: Files\Windows\Globalization was still untouched more than 24 h into the previous boot (+5 WCsc on the probe).
findings.fix: Call the control armable only if the WCsc rise is at least 50% of the entries the control listed and the 0x120089 handle rise roughly matches it. Have -Prepare prefer subtrees the repro measured as untouched late in a boot, such as Windows\Globalization.

findings.claim: The design record keeps a `dir /a /s` total of the store as the upper bound on excluded bytes ('run once'), but the design never says when or on which boot it runs. Run after the Restart and before the closing control, it spends the layer's first touch, VOIDs the session, and leaks about 210K entries. It also has the link-following problem from X3.
findings.evidence: Component 'Design record': "the excluded store's unmeasured size, with `dir /a /s` given as a reference upper bound only, run once, never added to a total". The run order does not include it.
findings.fix: Run it in -Prepare on the current, already-touched boot, with a walker that does not follow links, and store the total in the -Environment record.

findings.claim: Step 2 of Resolve 'opens the root and %ProgramData%' to map the store's final path. Under the Core.Tests override, the planted fake store is not under %ProgramData%. If step 2 still opens the real ProgramData, the 'junction or subst into the store' and 'subst spelling of a root above the store' cases resolve against the wrong anchor and either fail or pass without testing anything.
findings.evidence: Component: 'opens the root and %ProgramData% once each... maps the store's final path back'. 'In Core.Tests the store path comes from the internal ScanOptions.ContainerLayerStorePath override.'
findings.fix: Define step 2's second open as the parent of the store in use: the override's parent in tests, %ProgramData% otherwise. Never open the store itself.

findings.claim: The NotScanned row is rendered by UnreadableRows.Build, whose rows carry SL-088's 'Show in Explorer'. That action exists for 'folders the user cannot open'. On this row it opens Explorer with Layers selected, one double-click away from browsing the layer, which the documented workaround tells the user not to do. Each folder Explorer then lists spends first touch on its entries.
findings.evidence: Workaround: 'Do not browse Layers in Explorer or in the folder picker.' Commit 0f55300 (SL-088): "Make 'Show in Explorer' land on the right item... and on folders the user cannot open".
findings.fix: Leave 'Show in Explorer' off NotScanned rows. The kind is decided in Core and the App only maps kinds to words and actions, so this costs one mapping case.

dimensions_checked.result: X3: 'issued per sibling root' does not keep dir out of the store, because `dir /s` follows the All Users symlink to C:\ProgramData (schneegans.de; superuser 528487; SO 6913784). The cross-domain must-verify preconditions 3 and 4: if either fails, the WC* clause fails, and -Report has no outcome for it (X5). Recalled prior art (Windows-Sandbox#126): it ties leaks to each Sandbox session, which contradicts a linear ambient rate.

Y3: the closing control's ≥1 WC* threshold is too weak. Y4: where the `dir /a /s` bound runs is not stated. Y6: Show in Explorer appears on the NotScanned row. Root aliases (subst, 8.3, volume-GUID, the All Users symlink root) are handled by the two-step Resolve. Sibling names (Layers2, 'Layers.') are handled by the name gate plus full-path equality.

X2: the pressure step and its positive control (M3/N3) were dropped, so outcome C cannot tell cache from leak. The FolderDone exclusion plus the Core-decided Refused outcome holds by construction for every current walker. m4's backstop is moot without M6's counter.
none: the new EntryKind and Refused outcome follow answered questions (Q-179 through Q-182). PoolWatch's five modes and ScanArm's three are each used by the protocol, and the rig can be deleted.

X4: R0 is defined both before and after the Restart. X5: no route when the WC* or handle clause fails, and no UNDECIDED. Y5: under the test override, step 2 still opens %ProgramData%. The Refused outcome's contract (result value, exit 0, zero opens on the string path) is complete.

Covered by X5 (no outcome for null inputs or for a failed WC* clause). Resolve's failures (root unopenable, final-path call failing, ProgramData unresolved) fall back to the string verdict or None without throwing. Guard-stops count as over T.

Several dispositions that were accepted and are still owed are dropped without a reason: X1 (M5, m5), X2 (M3, N3), X5 (M6, m7, the tail of N2), Y1 (M4, m6), Y2 (N7, m3). Answered: m1, m2, N1's main hazard, N4, N6. Moot: N5 and m4.

X1: NotScanned shares the unreadable rows builder, and the report path is unspecified, so read-denied-folders and read-window are exposed again. Y2: the rule patterns lack (?m) and case-insensitivity, and the RunAs rule is gone. The new rules keeping the store-path override out of the rigs and the App are sound.

Core temp-tree cases are broad and never skipped: hardlink with a name inside the store, decoys, subst and \\?\, cancelled after the store, refuse, absent store, root unopenable. Missing: the m5 WindowCases case asserting the NotScanned report entry (X1). The zero-open refusal can be tested with a deny-ACL fake store, because falling through to step 2 would then give RootUnreadable.
none: there is no new input surface. The store-path override is internal and fitness-guarded out of the App and the rigs. The refusal message and the report fields expose nothing sensitive.
